title: Organotypic Culture of Adult Vascularized Porcine Retina Explants In Vitro on Nanotube Scaffolds
author: Friebe, Weigel, et al.
materials: Adult retina from porcine eyes was kindly provided by the slaughterhouse Emil Färber GmbH Großschlächterei & Co. KG, Belgern Schildau, Germany. Pigs were slaughtered at the age of 6 to 7 months and weighted approximately 100 to 150 kg. After individual electrocution and subsequent exsanguination, pig eyes were enucleated by a qualified butcher, leaving 3–5 mm of the optic nerve intact. Eyes were transferred to ice-cold PBS (4–8 °C, pH 7.4) and transported to the laboratory. Transportation took about 2 h. The eyeball was cleaned of surrounding tissue such as muscle, fatty tissue and connective tissue, transferred to a tube filled with 70% ethanol for some seconds to sterilize the ocular surface, washed twice in sterile PBS. The eye was opened along the ora serrata under sterile conditions in warmed culture medium. After disconnecting the vitreous body, the retina was always punched square (13 mm x 13 mm) centrally below the optic nerve. The quadratic punched samples were always taken from the same origin or position of the eye, separated from their surroundings, detached from the retinal pigment epithelium and carefully placed with the photoreceptor side down on the NTS and on the Millicell® cell culture inserts (hydrophilic PTFE-membrane, pore size 0.4 μm, PICM0RG50, Merck Millipore) for comparison purposes. Porcine retina was cultured using the air-liquid interface method as follows.

All steps were performed at room temperature. Living (non-PFA-fixed) retinal wholemounts were explanted and mechanically fixed on Whatman Filters with their vitread surface up, and placed into extracellular solution (136 mM NaCl, 3 mM KCl, 2 mM CaCl2, 1 MgCl2, 10 mM HEPES, 11 mM glucose), adjusted to pH 7.4. The wholemounts were loaded with vital dyes resolved in extracellular solution: 1 µM MitoTracker Orange (chloromethyltetramethylrosamine, M-7510, Invitrogen), CellTracker Green (5-chloromethylfluorescein diacetate; C-2925, Invitrogen) and FM™ 1–43 (Invitrogen). After appropriate incubation time, the wholemounts were transferred to a dye-free, extracellular solution filled chamber and examined using a confocal laser scanning microscope LSM 510 (Zeiss, Oberkochen, Germany) by viewing from the vitread side. The following cell membrane-permeant thiol-reactive vital dyes were tested: See Fig. 2, A-E; II and III.Fig. 2Morphology and viability of porcine retina at 0–6 h post mortem, symbolizing the effect of long transportation times from slaughter house to bench. Column I: hematoxylin/eosin staining of porcine retinas PFA-fixed at 0, 1, 3, 4 and 6 h post mortem. Column II: isolated living retinas incubated with in vivo fluorescent dye CellTracker Green (CTG), Müller glia cells were exclusively CTG positive and appear in green. Nerve fibers and ganglion cells somata (AII) appear black displaying no fluorescent staining. In E II a branched blood vessel is recognizable. Column III: retinas incubated with in vivo fluorescent dye MitoTracker Orange (MTO) and FM1-43 (green). MTO staines exclusively Müller cells and intact Müller cells/Müller cell end feet appear in orange. FM1-43 staines nerve fibers/ganglion cell axons and the cell membrane of ganglion cell somata. The distribution pattern of these in vivo fluorescent dyes are very specific and display the status of oxidative stress in the isolated retinal tissue. In E III (arrows) some ganglion cell somata were filled with FM1-43 showing the first damage of the integrity of the cell membrane due to oxidative stress. GC: ganglion cells, MC: Müller glial cells, NF: nerve fibers, BV: blood vessel

Porcine retinae was cultivated on two types of NT scaffolds (tube diameter 72 nm ± 3 nm and column 102 nm ± 5 nm) at 37 °C for 5 days. Retinae were fixed with 4%-PFA over night and carefully removed from NT scaffold. For immunohistological processing the tissue was embedded in 3% agarose (in PBS, pH 7.4). Samples were cut into 30 μm thin tissue slices using a vibratome and transferred into well-plates for staining process. The following steps were performed by using PBS (pH 7.4) + 1% DMSO + 3% triton-X-100, for incubation and washing. The slices were incubated in 5% donkey normal serum (Jackson Immunoresearch) for 1 h at room temperature and then incubated with primary antibody overnight at 4 °C (1:500 anti-GFAP by Dako; 1:100 anti-GαT1 by Santa Cruz; 1:100 anti-GαT2 by Santa Cruz, 1:500 anti-Glutmanine synthetase (GS) by Merck Millipore; 1:500 anti-IBA by Wako; 1:100 anti-PNA by Sigma; 1:500 anti-S100β by Sigma, 1:100 anti-Vimentin/V9 by Dako). After washing the slices 3 times for 1 h each, the fluorescent secondary antibodies (1:200, Jackson Immunoresearch) and Hoechst33358 (H3570, 1:1000, Life Technologies) were added and incubated for 2 h at room temperature and protected from light. Slices were washed, fixed and mounted on a microscope slide and stored upright until microscopic analysis using a confocal laser scanning microscope LSM 510 (Zeiss, Germany).

steps.title: Obtain and transport porcine eyes
steps.instruction: Acquire adult porcine eyes from a local slaughterhouse (pigs 6–7 months old, ~100–150 kg). After electrocution and exsanguination, enucleate eyes leaving 3–5 mm of optic nerve, place them in ice‑cold PBS (4–8 °C, pH 7.4) and transport to the laboratory within ~2 h.

steps.title: Sterilize and dissect retina explants
steps.instruction: Remove surrounding muscle, fat and connective tissue, dip the eye briefly (a few seconds) in 70 % ethanol, then wash twice in sterile PBS. Open the eye along the ora serrata in warmed culture medium, detach the vitreous body, and punch a central square retina piece (13 mm × 13 mm) below the optic nerve. Separate the retina from surrounding tissue and retinal pigment epithelium, then place it photoreceptor‑side down on either the nanotube scaffold (NTS) or a Millicell® insert (hydrophilic PTFE membrane, pore size 0.4 µm, PICM0RG50, Merck Millipore) for comparison.

steps.title: Place NTS and add medium
steps.instruction: Position the NTS on a sterile stainless‑steel grid (30 mm × 30 mm × 5 mm) inside a 5 cm diameter culture dish. Add Advanced DMEM/F‑12 supplemented with 0.1 % gentamycin, 10 % horse serum and 2 % Glutamax so that the medium contacts the bottom of the scaffold but does not overflow, allowing free gas exchange.

steps.title: Set up Millicell insert cultures
steps.instruction: Place the retina (photoreceptor side down) onto a Millicell® insert, insert it into a 5 cm diameter culture dish, and add culture medium until the filter is wet but not submerged.

steps.title: Incubate retina cultures
steps.instruction: Incubate both NTS and Millicell cultures at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for 5 days.

steps.title: Fix cultured retina and remove tissue
steps.instruction: Fix the retina on the NTS or insert with 4 % paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS (pH 7.4) for ≥4 h or overnight. For NTS, gently detach the tissue with a razor blade; for Millicell inserts, remove the tissue with a brush. Proceed to histological processing.

steps.title: Post‑mortem fixation of retina (time‑course)
steps.instruction: Keep whole eyes in ice‑cold PBS (4–8 °C) from enucleation until the desired post‑mortem time point (0, 1, 3, 4, 6 h). At each time point, dissect the retina as described above and fix immediately in 4 % PFA in PBS (pH 7.4) without further culture.

steps.title: Embed, slice and store retinal tissue
steps.instruction: Wash fixed retina samples in PBS (pH 7.4), embed in 3 % agarose (in PBS), and cut 30 µm sections with a vibratome. Store sections in PBS‑NaN₃ at 4 °C until staining.

steps.title: Hematoxylin‑eosin staining of sections
steps.instruction: Mount sections on microscope slides, dry on a heating plate at 35 °C until even, then desalinate in distilled water. Apply hematoxylin for 4 min, wash three times with water over 30 min, apply eosin for 4 min, rinse in distilled water, then 80 % ethanol, and finally distilled water until agarose is clear. Remove excess water, dry on a heating plate, add mounting medium, cover with a coverslip, and store slides upright at room temperature protected from light for 24–48 h before microscopy (Keyence BZ‑9000).

steps.title: Vital dye labeling of living wholemounts
steps.instruction: Perform all steps at room temperature. Explant living retinal wholemounts, mount vitread side up on Whatman filters, and immerse in extracellular solution (136 mM NaCl, 3 mM KCl, 2 mM CaCl₂, 1 mM MgCl₂, 10 mM HEPES, 11 mM glucose, pH 7.4). Load with 1 µM MitoTracker Orange (M‑7510, Invitrogen), CellTracker Green (C‑2925, Invitrogen) and FM 1‑43 (Invitrogen) dissolved in the same solution; incubate for the appropriate time. Transfer wholemounts to a dye‑free chamber containing extracellular solution and image from the vitread side using a Zeiss LSM 510 confocal laser scanning microscope.

steps.title: Immunohistochemical staining of retinal slices
steps.instruction: Culture retinae on two nanotube scaffold types (tube diameter 72 nm ± 3 nm; column diameter 102 nm ± 5 nm) at 37 °C for 5 days, then fix with 4 % PFA overnight and remove from scaffold. Embed in 3 % agarose (PBS, pH 7.4), cut 30 µm slices with a vibratome, and place slices in well plates. Block in PBS (pH 7.4) containing 1 % DMSO and 3 % Triton‑X‑100 with 5 % donkey normal serum (Jackson Immunoresearch) for 1 h at room temperature. Incubate with primary antibodies overnight at 4 °C (1:500 anti‑GFAP, Dako; 1:100 anti‑GαT1, Santa Cruz; 1:100 anti‑GαT2, Santa Cruz; 1:500 anti‑glutamine synthetase, Merck Millipore; 1:500 anti‑IBA, Wako; 1:100 anti‑PNA, Sigma; 1:500 anti‑S100β, Sigma; 1:100 anti‑vimentin/V9, Dako). Wash three times for 1 h each with the same PBS/DMSO/Triton‑X‑100 solution. Incubate with fluorescent secondary antibodies (1:200, Jackson Immunoresearch) and Hoechst 33358 (1:1000, Life Technologies) for 2 h at room temperature protected from light. Wash, fix, mount on slides, store upright until analysis with a Zeiss LSM 510 confocal microscope.
